featured_reviews.review_text:
I ordered veg biryani from Taste of Kerala on 13 October 2025, but I was delivered chicken biryani instead. This is a serious issue, especially for someone who does not eat non-veg.
I immediately went to the restaurant and showed them the delivered order. They said the owner was not present and asked me to return the food and come back the next day for a refund. I trusted them and handed over the food.
When I returned the next day, the owner refused to take responsibility and told me to contact Zomato instead. This was extremely unprofessional and dishonest.
This is not just a mistake—it’s a serious concern when non-veg food is served while claiming it is veg. Please be very careful. If the intention was to avoid a refund, they could have been honest instead of wasting my time.
I do not recommend this restaurant.

featured_reviews.name: Rituka Nakhawa
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited Taste of Kerala and had a really good experience overall. The place serves tasty, authentic food with nice service. Due to the crowd, the staff does struggle a bit with serving everyone on time, but they still manage with a positive attitude.
We tried the Sunday Special Veg Banana Meal, Coconut Chilly Roasted Chicken with Kerala Paratha, and Chicken Kizhi Parotha. Every dish was absolutely delicious — rich flavours and true Kerala taste. We’ll definitely be visiting again!
A special mention to the manager, who was extremely warm and attentive. He personally checked on every table, and when he noticed we enjoyed the payasam, he even served us some extra. Such gestures really make the experience memorable. 💛🌴✨

featured_reviews.name: Hozefa Topiwala
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Taste of Kerala is truly a hidden gem! The place has a simple, no-frills setup — the ground floor is non-AC while the mezzanine floor is AC, though the ceiling upstairs is a bit low and seating is quite basic. But once the food arrives, you forget everything else!

The service here is absolutely fantastic. We were served by Raki, who was super enthusiastic and guided us through the menu with genuine passion. The restaurant is really lucky to have such a dedicated person on their team.

We ordered Chicken Pachamolak, Chicken Kerala, and Prawn Ghee Roast with wheat Laccha Kerala Paratha, and every dish was lip-smacking delicious. The authentic Kerala flavors were spot on!

They also serve complimentary Kerala papad, dahi boondi salad, and a variety of authentic chutneys, which are a must-try and perfectly complement the meal.

Overall, an amazing experience — fantastic food, warm service, and great value for money. We’ll definitely be visiting again and again!

featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ 5/5

If you’re in Fort and craving authentic South Indian food, JM Idli Cafe is an absolute must-visit! It’s one of those rare places that combine delicious food, warm service, and genuine consistency — a true gem in the heart of Mumbai.

I’ve visited JM Idli Cafe multiple times, and every experience has been wonderful. Their menu offers a perfect blend of traditional South Indian favourites and creative variations. But the dish that truly wins my heart every single time is their Mysore Sada Cheese Dosa. It’s absolutely fantastic! The dosa is crisp, golden, and perfectly balanced — the slight spice of the Mysore chutney mixed with the smooth, melted cheese creates a unique and addictive flavour. You can immediately tell it’s made with care and fresh ingredients.

Their idlis are soft and fluffy, the sambar has that comforting homemade taste, and their chutneys are fresh, vibrant, and perfectly seasoned. Even simple dishes like the ghee dosa, upma, and pongal are prepared with attention to detail and taste just right.

The staff here deserve full appreciation as well — they’re polite, attentive, and always serve with a smile. You never have to wait too long, and they make sure every customer feels valued.

The café itself is clean, cosy, and welcoming — perfect for breakfast, lunch, or even a light evening meal. The prices are very reasonable for the quality and portion sizes, which makes it even more worth it.

Overall, JM Idli Cafe is the kind of place that keeps you coming back. Every visit feels satisfying and cheerful. If you love South Indian food or simply enjoy delicious, freshly made meals, you’ll love this spot. And if you visit, don’t miss their Mysore Sada Cheese Dosa — it’s honestly one of the best in Mumbai!

"Prabhu Pure Veg" in Masjid Bunder, Mumbai, is a well-established vegetarian restaurant with a history dating back to 1944. It's known for its economical pricing, convenient location near Masjid Bunder Railway Station, and a variety of pure vegetarian dishes.
Here's a detailed review based on common feedback:
Overall Experience:
Prabhu Pure Veg generally receives positive reviews for its value for money and tasty, hygienic food. It's a popular spot for locals and those seeking a quick, satisfying vegetarian meal in the bustling Masjid Bunder area. While not a fine-dining establishment, it serves its purpose as a reliable and budget-friendly option.
Food Quality and Variety:
* Taste: The food is consistently praised for being delicious and well-prepared. Many reviewers highlight the good quality and reasonable rates.
* Specialties: While specific "must-try" dishes aren't overwhelmingly mentioned, items like Ghee Podi Idli, Batata Wada, and Lemon Grass Tea have been positively noted. Their menu is described as extensive, covering various vegetarian preparations from local and potentially global influences. South Indian, North Indian, and Street Food options are commonly available.
* Hygiene: The restaurant is generally considered to maintain good hygiene standards, which is a significant factor for many diners.
* Ingredients: The focus is on using quality ingredients from trusted suppliers, which contributes to the overall taste and freshness of the dishes.
Pricing:
* Economical: One of Prabhu Pure Veg's strongest points is its affordability. With an average price for two around ₹450, it's considered very budget-friendly, especially for the portion sizes and quality offered.
Service:
* Mixed Reviews: Service can be a mixed bag. While some reviews mention prompt and good service, others specifically point out slow service and long wait times, particularly during peak hours. This seems to be an area where improvement is often suggested.
* Staff: Some reviews note the staff as polite and well-mannered.
Ambience:
* Casual and Functional: Prabhu Pure Veg is a casual dining restaurant. It's not typically known for its elaborate ambiance but rather for being a functional place to grab a quick meal. It can get crowded, especially due to its popularity and location.
* Presentation: While the ambiance might be simple, some reviewers appreciate the presentation of the food itself.
Location:
* Convenient: Its proximity to Masjid Bunder Railway Station ticket bridge and Bhaat Bazar makes it easily accessible for commuters and shoppers in the area.
Things to Consider:
* Wait Times: Be prepared for potential wait times, especially if visiting during busy hours.
* Simple Ambiance: Don't expect a luxurious or fancy dining experience. It's more of a no-frills, focus-on-the-food kind of place.
* Crowds: Due to its popularity and location, it can be quite busy and noisy.
In Summary:
Prabhu Pure Veg is a highly recommended spot for those looking for economical, tasty, and hygienic pure vegetarian food in the Masjid Bunder area of Mumbai. It's a no-frills establishment that prioritizes good food at affordable prices, making it a local favorite. While service speed can sometimes be an issue, the overall positive feedback on food quality and value makes it a worthwhile visit for any vegetarian food enthusiast.

featured_reviews.name: Ayush Bhandari
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re looking for a spot where traditional South Indian soul meets a modern, aesthetic vibe, Malgudi in Lower Parel is a masterclass in culinary harmony. Curated by the legendary Shankar Mahadevan, the restaurant feels less like a typical eatery and more like a carefully composed melody—vibrant, comforting, and full of character.
The ambience hits you first; it’s thoughtfully designed with a clean, aesthetic appeal that makes it perfect for a relaxed weekend brunch or a stylish dinner.
The Food: From Classic to Creative
The menu takes you on a journey through Karnataka and beyond, elevating humble staples into gourmet experiences.
Podi Cheese Balls: The spice of the podi cuts through the richness of the cheese, creating a crunchy, gooey delight that’s hard to stop at just one.
Ghee Podi Thate Idli: This was a standout. The idli was incredibly soft, acting as the perfect canvas for the fragrant, nutty podi and a generous dousing of ghee.
Davangere Benne Podi Dosa: True to its roots, this dosa was buttery (*benne*) and crisp, with the podi adding a layer of depth that reminded us why this regional specialty is so iconic.
Mulbagal Legacy Cheese Masala Dosa: The addition of cheese modernized the legacy recipe without overshadowing the traditional masala. Beverages:
Mango Berry Matcha: A vibrant, fruity twist on matcha that felt light and refreshing—a great palate cleanser between the buttery dosas.
Coconut Cold Brew Coffee: Smooth and tropical. The natural sweetness of the coconut milk paired beautifully with the bold kick of the cold brew.
Desserts:
You cannot leave without trying the Filter Kaffi Panna Cotta. It’s a brilliant nod to South Indian coffee culture, with a silky texture and a deep caffeine punch. The Chocolate Pull-Up Cake added a bit of "Instagrammable" drama to the table—decadent, rich, and the perfect end for any chocolate lover.

Malgudi isn't just about the name behind it; the food truly speaks for itself. It captures the "Legacy" of South India while dressing it up for the modern Lower Parel.

featured_reviews.name: Sagar Abichandani
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (4/5)

Ramashray in Matunga is one of those classic South Indian institutions that still feels properly “Bombay” – bustling, no-nonsense and absolutely focused on the food. I dropped in specifically to try their ghee podi Thatte idli and walked out very happy (and very full).

The ghee podi Thatte idli is easily the hero of the menu. The idli itself is thick and soft – that perfect Thatte style – with a beautiful fermented flavour. It comes drenched in ghee, with a generous ring of podi that clings to every bite. The texture, temperature and seasoning were spot on; this is the kind of dish you could reorder without thinking twice.

The pineapple sheera was another standout. Warm, fragrant and not cloyingly sweet, with enough pineapple to cut through the richness of ghee – it felt like a proper old-school dessert, the kind you’d expect from a place that’s been doing this for decades. If you have a sweet tooth, this is non-negotiable.

Where the experience dipped a bit for me was the masala dosa. For a place with Ramashray’s reputation, I expected a benchmark dosa, but it was underwhelming:
•	The dosa was small in size compared to typical Matunga standards.
•	The texture lacked crispness – instead of that satisfying crunch, the dosa kept crumbling even when handled gently, which made it messy and not very enjoyable.
•	The masala itself was decent, but the base failed to carry it.

Service is fast, efficient and very typical of old-school South Indian joints in Mumbai – you’re seated, served and cleared quickly, which works well given the constant rush. Prices are reasonable for the quality, and the overall vibe is nostalgic: crowded, lively, with conversations, steel plates and filter coffee aromas all blending into one.

Overall, Ramashray still deserves its cult status for certain dishes, especially the ghee podi Thatte idli and pineapple sheera, which I would come back for in a heartbeat. I’m giving it 4 stars only because the masala dosa – usually the litmus test at a South Indian eatery – fell short on texture and portion size. Fix that, and this would easily be a 5-star experience.

Malgudi: Great Vibes, Confused Kitchen & Extra Fees
Let’s be real—I wanted to love this place. Walking into Malgudi on SV Road, the vibe is immaculate. It sets you up for a cozy, authentic South Indian experience. But between the kitchen confusion and the final bill, it’s a bit of a rollercoaster.
Here is the unfiltered breakdown:
The Star of the Show
If you go here, do yourself a favor and order the Benne Masala Dosa. It was genuinely too good—crispy, buttery, and exactly what you hope for. The chutney pairing was also on point and very tasty.
The "What happened here?" Section
Unfortunately, the rest of the meal felt like an identity crisis.
• The Sambar Situation: This was weird. The sambar actually tasted different across different dishes. Consistency is key, guys—pick a lane!
• Portions & Options: The menu feels very limited, and the portion sizes are basically a tease. For the price, you expect to leave full, not looking for a snack on the way home.
• Overall Taste: Aside from the Benne Dosa, the general taste could really be improved. It feels like they are holding back flavor.
The Coffee Letdown
For a place with this vibe, you expect the coffee game to be strong. It wasn't.
• Coffee Mocktails: Hard pass. They just felt not worth the price tag.
• Filter Coffee: The ultimate test for a South Indian spot, and they failed it. It tasted average at best and definitely lacked that authentic "kick" you crave.
The Final Pinch
Just when you are questioning the portion sizes vs. the price, the bill arrives. They levy a 5% Service Charge.
Paying extra for "service" when the filter coffee is average and the sambar is inconsistent? That stings.
The Verdict
Go for the Benne Masala Dosa and the aesthetic, but lower your expectations for everything else. It’s a great place to sit, but be ready to pay a premium (plus 5%) for a mixed bag of flavors.

featured_reviews.name: Miura
featured_reviews.review_text:
As expected from such an old and iconic restaurant, the place carries a beautiful old-world charm. The crowd was immense, and we had to wait nearly 30–45 minutes for a table. Seating is shared with other guests, which adds to the authentic traditional dining experience.

What truly stood out was the remarkably quick and efficient service despite the rush. We ordered dosa and filter coffee — the dosa was absolutely delicious, especially with the generous layer of fresh white butter that elevated the taste beautifully. The filter coffee was equally excellent and perfectly satisfying.

The restaurant is quite pocket-friendly, and the staff deserves appreciation for being extremely prompt, supportive, and well-managed amidst the heavy crowd. The only downside is the waiting time and constant rush; otherwise, everything about the experience was wonderful.

featured_reviews.name: Neel
featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Madras is one of the most iconic South Indian restaurants in Mumbai and truly lives up to its reputation. Located in the heart of Matunga, this place is famous for serving authentic and delicious South Indian food with consistent quality for decades. The moment you enter, the aroma of fresh filter coffee, ghee, and spices creates a warm and nostalgic feeling.
I tried their famous dosa and idli, and both were excellent. The dosa was perfectly crispy with a flavorful potato filling, while the idli was soft, fresh, and served with tasty chutneys and sambhar. Their filter coffee was another highlight — strong, aromatic, and refreshing. Despite being crowded most of the time, the service is quick and efficient, which is impressive.
The restaurant maintains cleanliness and has a simple yet traditional atmosphere that adds to the experience. Prices are also reasonable considering the quality and popularity of the food. Overall, Cafe Madras is a must-visit place for anyone who loves authentic South Indian cuisine. It perfectly combines taste, tradition, and quality, making every visit memorable.
